messages:
incident-bot: PAGED: apigw-prod - elevated 5xx (502/504) across edge -> spike detected at 08:12 UTC. Alert: apigw.errors.5xx.rate > 3% for 5m. See: https://alerts.redwood.example/INC-4729998880 :rotating_light:
Anna_oncall: Ack. Jumping in. Anyone seeing scope by region/service?
sam_eng: Seeing big spike from eu-west and na-east. p95 latency up from 120ms -> 1.4s, error rate ~6% in eu-west. Funnel shows fanout to inference-gateway pods, 502/504 primarily from upstream timeouts.
Maria_sre: Logs show repeated `upstream read timeout` from mux-proxy -> inference pool. Also seeing connection resets from one backend ASG.
Anna_oncall: Thx. Immediate mitigation ideas: 1) enable region fallback routing for eu-west traffic to na-east (gentle shift) 2) increase backend timeout / disable strict keepalive for problematic pool 3) circuit-break heavy clients. Any objections? :thinking_face:
Sam_eng: Agree. Kicking a quick traffic-shift (50% -> na-east) for 10m to see behavior. Running command now:```
# ephemeral run: route-shift --from eu-west --to na-east --percent 50 --duration 10m
Tracing: route-shift: started (run-id: rs-4729)
```
Kate_pm: Heads-up - Support reports ~12 customer errors in last 10m, mostly enterprise customers in EU. I'm posting a brief to CSMs. Any ETA on stabilization?
Support_bot: Ticket 48721 created: customer "FinServe" reported API timeouts. Link: https://support.redwood.example/t/48721
Maria_sre: After shift, eu-west error rate dropped to ~3.2% and na-east increased slightly but within SLO. Still seeing a noisy backend instance (i-0a1b2c3d) with high TCP retransmits. I propose cordon+replace that instance in inference pool.
Anna_oncall: Good catch. Sam, can you drain that instance?
sam_eng: Starting drain now:```
kubectl cordon node/i-0a1b2c3d && kubectl drain node/i-0a1b2c3d --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
# monitoring pods rescheduled
```
Anna_oncall: Also toggled increase of upstream timeout from 1.5s -> 3s as temporary measure (will revert after stabilization). Command shown: `set-config apigw.upstream_timeout=3000ms --ephemeral`
Maria_sre: Noted. After drain & timeout bump, eu-west 5xx down to 0.9%, p95 back to 180ms. No further customer escalations in last 8m.
Kate_pm: I'll update CSMs, ask Support to hold on formal customer notice until we confirm 15m stable.
Support_bot: Escalation update posted to ticket 48721.
Anna_oncall: Quick postmortem notes: probable root-cause: single unhealthy backend instance (TCP issues) + aggressive upstream timeout config. Mitigation chain: traffic shift, timeout bump, drain unhealthy instance. Next steps: replace instance, roll through similar hosts in ASG, revert timeout to baseline after 30m stable, follow-up RCA.
Sam_eng: Replacement initiated (auto-scale group replacement triggered).
Maria_sre: Adding short-term alert tweak: increase detection threshold for spiky short-lived blips to avoid noisy pages; create a separate pager category for sustained >5m. I'll open a PR.
Anna_oncall: Handoff: I'll stay on until 09:00 UTC and then hand to night on-call @mike. Please add any follow-ups to this thread.
Kate_pm: Thanks all. I'll coordinate customer comms if we see more.
Support_bot: Logged incident summary and linked tickets: https://incidents.redwood.example/4729998880
Anna_oncall: Final check - last check: p95 170ms, 5xx 0.7% global, eu-west 0.8%. Marking incident as mitigated for now. Will run post-incident RCA doc. :white_check_mark:
